nodes.text: Let $G$ be either $Q_3$ or $K_{3,3}$ or $H_5$ (the last formed by adding two vertex-disjoint chords to $C_5$). Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then\[R(G,H)\ll m?\]

#567 : [EFRS93] [Er95,p.177] graph theory | ramsey theory In other words, is $G$ Ramsey size linear? A special case of [566] . In [Er95] Erdős specifically asks about the case $G=K_{3,3}$. The graph $H_5$ can also be described as $K_4^*$, obtained from $K_4$ by subdividing one edge. ($K_4$ itself is not Ramsey size linear, since $R(4,n)\gg n^{3-o(1)}$, see [166] .) Bradać, Gishboliner, and Sudakov [BGS23] have shown that every subdivision of $K_4$ on at least $6$ vertices is Ramsey size linear, and also that $R(H_5,H) \ll m$ whenever $H$ is a bipartite graph with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices. This problem is #32 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
